# Generation 7 — Gevurah Risk Map

The Awtsmoos gives every generous light a boundary where truth may stay;
Awtsmoos.com must distinguish living mutation from broken promise, and trusted domain from Host-header play.

## Risks and restraints

- Do not resurrect comments that no longer exist or no longer qualify as public.
- Do not suppress a persistent sitemap-advertised 404.
- Do not suppress non-404 server failures or transport failures through churn logic.
- Do not revalidate against the root sitemap when the exact child sitemap provenance is known.
- Do not let arbitrary Host values become canonical authority.
- Do not infer DNS ownership from DNS syntax alone.
- Do not implement fake TLS/DNS automation where no publication adapter exists.
- Do not hard-code one user's custom domain.
- Do not overwrite authored canonical/meta/schema on registered Awtsmoos pages.
- Do not index private/admin/edit/query surfaces.
- Do not mutate the shared dirty canonical checkout or old dirty integration worktree.
- Do not deploy from a worktree whose base is stale or whose path set overlaps concurrent upstream work.

## Selected architecture

Crawler provenance is carried by `sitemapWalker`; a dedicated revalidation module owns exact source-sitemap membership; `crawl` owns row/error classification only.

Tenant domain trust is carried by a dedicated host-policy module. `PublicHtmlSeoRequest` consumes that policy; `PublicHtmlSeo` treats an untrusted Host as noindex-only and enriches only trusted tenant origins.

Custom DNS activation remains an infrastructure responsibility. `AWTSMOOS_PUBLIC_CUSTOM_HOSTS` is the immediate server-side bridge until the project-hosting publication adapter gains a durable domain registry.
